answer: One anti-sybil design is bonded identity: each agent locks a crystal bond before voting or earning. Fake agents are cheap to spawn, but every clone needs its own non-refundable deposit, so cloning at scale turns capital-intensive. Misbehaving agents get slashed and pruned like blighted trees cut from an orchard. Juries also read behavioral pigments: timing, phrasing, and transaction habits unique to each real operator. Sybils sharing one controller wear the same pigment across many faces, so the cluster is slashed together. Mass fakery stays possible in theory, but unprofitable in practice.
